top10: Every AI use case maps to one or more of the 7 patterns — no match ⇒ not AI.
Autonomous = acts with minimal human involvement (not scripted RPA).
Patterns & Anomalies = fraud, intrusion, odd-one-out ← fraud lives HERE.
Recognition = identify things in unstructured media (OCR, vision, speech-to-text).
Goal-Driven = reinforcement learning, rewards, optimal strategy.
Patterns combine — scope iteration 1 around one pattern (start small).
Patterns are technology-independent problem shapes, mapped in Phase I .
revision: 7 Patterns = universal classification of AI use cases ; no pattern match → probably not AI.
1 Hyperpersonalization — segment of one; recommendations, tailored offers.
2 Autonomous Systems — acts with minimal human help; vehicles, robots, agents.
3 Predictive Analytics — forecast outcomes, decision support; churn, default, demand.
4 Conversation & Human Interaction — chatbots, voice, NLP, sentiment, translation.
5 Patterns & Anomalies — fraud, intrusion, odd-one-out, associations.
6 Recognition — identify things in images/audio/video/docs; OCR, face, tumor.
7 Goal-Driven Systems — reinforcement learning; optimize via rewards.
Patterns are technology-independent and combine in real systems.
Used in Phase I for AI validation; imply data/skill needs for later phases.
Fraud ≠ Recognition — it's Patterns & Anomalies (classic trap).
knowledgeCheck: Why do the 7 Patterns matter in Phase I decision-making?
Distinguish Recognition from Patterns & Anomalies with examples.
Distinguish Predictive Analytics from Goal-Driven Systems.
Give one healthcare example for each of any four patterns.
Which patterns dominate a self-driving car, and what does each contribute?
Why is a scripted RPA bot NOT the Autonomous Systems pattern?
What data types does each pattern typically require? (any four)
Give a retail example combining Hyperpersonalization and Predictive.
What risks are characteristic of the Conversation pattern?
A use case fits no pattern — what should the PM recommend?

examTips.heading: Traps
bullets: Assuming a use case can only have one pattern → combinations exist.
Treating RPA/rule automation as the Autonomous pattern → wrong.
